correctness.rationale: For each fixed finite integer frequency set, Parseval q-fold convolution yields the even-p majorant, with equality phase relations generated by a finite lattice basis for sufficiently large q. Global maximizing amplitudes converge to the flat unit vector because the sharp L∞ limit is √m. Positive coefficients have exactly gcd-many nondegenerate peaks; uniform twice-amplitude-differentiable Laplace expansion gives the sharp log-norm coefficient and perturbative Hessian. Negative tangent identity Hessian provides the unique optimal amplitude and explicit 1/p frequency-variance drift. The packaged standard-library checker passed 216 finite assertions; infinite statements rely on the analytical proof.

value.rationale: The sharp finite-aperture Fourier synthesis norm is a natural harmonic-analysis invariant; the new Gaussian variance coefficient separates frequency geometries and the universal vector correction quantifies how the *optimized* coefficients concentrate away from spectral outliers as the moment exponent grows. Proving global optimized-amplitude uniqueness and eventual exact phase rigidity across every finite integer aperture is stronger than the standard L∞ bound or fixed-vector Laplace asymptotics; it can inform finite spectral synthesis design and high-moment extremizer analysis. All claims are scoped to fixed apertures, so no unsupported uniform bandwidth or general-exponent significance is asserted.
